title: The LOKLOK Platform: Architecture and Implementation
paragraphs: Chapter 4 The LOKLOK Platform: Architecture and Implementation Chapter abstract. This chapter describes LOKLOK: the Broadcaster Reputation Score, MORE diversity-constrained recommendation, propaganda detection and moderation, the ERIC governance loop, and the measurement surface. It presents the eld interface and explains how BRS, credibility intervals, the Echo Meter, and the survey ow appeared to participants. It separates implemented mechanisms from claims about deployment and usage. LOKLOK is the proposed operational platform for this research programme. Its implementation account describes a Go backend, mobile client, and web interface. The following chapter distinguishes proposed reference mechanisms, reported implementation behavior, and requirements for experimental delity. Neither a platform feature nor a mathematical analogy establishes an EST proposition without a suitable test. 58

CHAPTER 4. THE LOKLOK PLATFORM: ARCHITECTURE AND IMPLEMENTATION 59 4.1 Implementation Fidelity and the Scope of the BRS The inherited implementation account describes distinct scoring models. Its sourceinspection report identies a BRS.Update function called by a feedback service; that source tree is absent from the present archive and these claims have not been reveried. It accumulates a scalar rating through a weighted beta-shaped state: at+1 = at + wtrt, bt+1 = bt + wt(1 −rt), bBt+1 = at+1 at+1 + bt+1 . (4.1) In ordinary terms: the two counters accumulate favourable and unfavourable fractions of feedback. Their ratio produces the displayed score. For example, a rating of .8 with weight 1 adds .8 to the rst counter and .2 to the second. This arithmetic does not turn audience approval into truth. Here a0, b0 > 0, wt ≥0, and rt ∈[0, 1] are required. A ve-star input is not already on this scale; its actual mapping, prior, and weighting policy must be checked in the version used for any experiment. Fractional or weighted increments can dene a useful pseudocount score, but do not by themselves establish a calibrated Bayesian posterior about factual credibility. An interval based on these counts describes the assumed scoring model, not automatically the accuracy of a broadcaster's claims. The feedback service starts new states at (a0, b0) = (2, 2). Its reported interval clips the normal approximation bB ± 1.96 p Var(B) to [0, 1]; it is not an exact beta-quantile interval. The evidence eld a+b includes prior mass and weights, so it is not a respondent count. A separate score route persists the component smoother Bt+1 = clip[0,1]{Bt + η[.40Rt + .35It + .25St −Bt]}. It neither updates the beta state

Broadcast Rigor is specied as a combination of streaming activity, audience retention, and schedule consistency: Brig u (t) = σ Z t 0 e−λ(t−τ)[α1 StreamHours + α2 Lretention + α3 δ−1 schedule] dτ . (4.2) In ordinary terms: the proposed rule accumulates streaming activity, retention, and schedule consistency, discounts older information, then maps the total to a bounded score. These inputs must be dened on compatible scales as functions of τ; δschedule must be positive. Activity and retention alone do not establish broadcast rigor. Social Validation is a PageRank-style trust score with a bounded endorsement cap W capped vu = min(Wvu, ¯W/(1 + βBv)) intended to limit Matthew-eect concentration, and a Gini trigger G(t) > 0.40 that activates a freshers boost for underrecognised new broadcasters. Information Quality is the quality-weighted entropy of the source set with

CHAPTER 4. THE LOKLOK PLATFORM: ARCHITECTURE AND IMPLEMENTATION 62 a correction-term bonus: Binf u (t) = HQ(Su) + γ · CorrMadeu TimeToCorru · CommValidu . (4.3) In ordinary terms: the reference expression combines a source-set summary with a correction term. More corrections increase that term and longer correction delays reduce it, all else equal. As written, a larger CommValid denominator also reduces it; this does not automatically reward stronger community validation. The earlier specication therefore needs a justied denition and directional check before implementation. The correction term requires a dened scale and positive denominators; it must not reward a broadcaster simply for producing more errors to correct. These safeguards are design requirements, not eects established by the eld questionnaire. The three components are aggregated using career-phase weights: Bu(t) = w(t)⊤Bu(t). The vector w(t) transitions from (0.6, 0.2, 0.2)⊤ for new broadcasters to (0.2, 0.5, 0.3)⊤for established ones. These weights are design parameters, not estimates from the audience survey. The interface is intended to display uncertainty alongside the point score. A beta posterior would require an appropriate likelihood and prior; a normal interval of the form ˆB ± 1.96 SE( ˆB) is a dierent construction and cannot simply be called a beta-conjugate credibility interval. Neither the reported CFA summaries nor the questionnaire alpha establishes a calibrated

CHAPTER 4. THE LOKLOK PLATFORM: ARCHITECTURE AND IMPLEMENTATION 63 interval for the algorithmic BRS. The implementation should dene its score scale, likelihood, and uncertainty method before consequential use. 4.3 Recommendation with Diversity Constraints (MORE) The Multi-Objective Recommendation Engine ranks candidate content by a weighted combination of user value and diversity, subject to a fairness budget. User value combines the propaganda-adjusted probability of the item with the broadcaster's BRS: UVS(c, u) = PDTS(c, u) · Bc · (1 −Pprop(c)). (4.4) In plain terms. The utility score ranks candidate broadcasts by expected value, diversity, and a penalty term. It is the app's "what should I show next" rule. 4.3.1 Time-Resolved Attentional Coherence: A Zewail-Inspired Formal Analogy The quantity PDTS(c, u) in Equation (4.4) requires an explicit denition. A commuter with the radio application running is not necessarily attending to the broadcast: the phone may be playing in the background while the rider talks, checks messages, or watches trac. The present framework therefore treats attention as a time-resolved coupling state between a listener u and a broadcast c, rather than as a synonym for ride duration or application presence. The formal inspiration is Ahmed H. Zewail's femtochemistry, recognised by

CHAPTER 4. THE LOKLOK PLATFORM: ARCHITECTURE AND IMPLEMENTATION 64 the 1999 Nobel Prize in Chemistry. In pumpprobe spectroscopy, a pump pulse launches a coherent wavepacket at t0; a delayed probe pulse measures the transitionstate population at t0 +∆t before vibrational dephasing destroys coherence (Zewail, 1999, 2000). The analogy used here is deliberately formal: it supplies a principled way to model a short-lived attentional window, not a claim that social listening obeys physical thermodynamics or chemical kinetics. Let tpump be the timestamp of a broadcast inection cue (a claim assertion, a topic shift, or a source prompt), and let tprobe = tpump + ∆tu,c be the listener's foreground interaction, telemetry ping, or EMA Layer-1 response. The pumpprobe attentional coherence gate is PDTS(c, u, ∆t) = exp −∆tu,c τdephase,u | {z } coherence decay · exp −Edistract(u, t) Tcog,u | {z } ride-distraction barrier · 1 2 [1 + cos ∆ϕu,c(t)] | {z } phase locking , (4.5) where τdephase,u > 0 is the listener's dephasing time, Edistract is ambient transit friction (trac noise, multi-tasking, conversation), Tcog is the listener's cognitive engagement energy, and ∆ϕu,c(t) is the phase dierence between the broadcast cadence and the listener's foreground focus. The gate lies in [0, 1]: an active, phase-locked listener probed within the coherence window has PDTS →1; a phone left playing in the background for several minutes has PDTS →0. The numerical values used in the simulation are declared design parameters, not measured chemical quantities. In plain terms. The gate is a formal way to say three common-sense things. First, attention fades as time passes. Second, a noisy or distracting ride lowers attention. Third, attention is stronger when the broadcast rhythm and the listener focus are

CHAPTER 4. THE LOKLOK PLATFORM: ARCHITECTURE AND IMPLEMENTATION 65 aligned. The equation multiplies these three factors, so any one of them can switch attention o. Figure 4.1: The Zewail-inspired pumpprobe attentional coherence gate. The diagram is a formal analogy: the broadcast inection cue is the pump, the EMA probe is the delayed measurement, and dephasing represents loss of foreground attention during a ride. It is not a claim that social listening is a chemical process. The gate enters the model in three places. First, it multiplies the retention term in the broadcaster-rigour update so that passive background play cannot inate apparent exposure. Second, it scales the evidence anchor used by the DeGroot reputation update. Third, it modulates engagement and the latent credibility trajectory. Figure 4.2 shows the resulting decay curves and the active-versus-passive contrast. The implementation is included in loklok_pipeline.py (Section K), so the analogy is auditable rather than purely rhetorical. Interpretive boundary. The Zewail analogy is used because it makes the temporal structure of attention explicit and falsiable: if the gate has no eect on retention, reputation, or ratings, the mechanism should be removed. It does not

Panel A: coherence decay for phase-locked, partial, and decoupled attention; the 12-second active probe and the 180-second passive background case are marked. Panel B: coherence across dephasing regimes. The empirical eld wave does not contain the timestamped telemetry needed to estimate τdephase; that parameter remains a model assumption and a target for future platform-in-the-loop measurement. Gate ablation. To test whether the gate is doing any work, the main simulator was rerun with the gate o, with a simple exponential decay, and with half and double the dephasing time, holding personas and seed xed. The full gate gives ∆SReval = +0.827 [0.779, 0.875]. Turning the gate o raises the contrast by +0.194 [0.127, 0.260] and the competence gain by about 3.25 points; replacing it with a simple exponential decay raises the contrast by +0.110 [0.043, 0.177]. The full gate is therefore not inert, and its distraction/phase terms carry structure beyond a simple decay. The baseline gate is open in only about 15.4% of personasession slots, so the gate is a strong attentional lter, not a minor adjustment. It reduces

This is a model-internal ablation, not a human test of the pumpprobe analogy; no empirical estimate of the dephasing time exists in the eld wave. Diversity is measured as the cosine dissimilarity of the item from the user's recent consumption vector, DBI(c, u) = 1 −cos(vc, Crec). The engine solves the constrained optimisation c∗= arg max c∈C (w1 · UVS + w2 · DBI) s.t. |SAI| ≤Bmax, (4.6) In plain terms. MORE chooses a slate that balances relevance and diversity. The diversity weight is the dial: turn it up and the slate becomes broader but less tailored. In ordinary terms: choose the item with the highest weighted value and diversity score among candidates meeting the declared balance constraint. The weights determine the trade-o; the constraint determines eligibility. This is a proposed decision rule, not evidence that a deployed feed enforces it. where SAI is a demographic-balance index and Bmax the bias budget. The

CHAPTER 4. THE LOKLOK PLATFORM: ARCHITECTURE AND IMPLEMENTATION 68 Echo Meter Rt is updated after each recommendation, Rt ←(1 −αR)Rt−1 + αR(1 − DBI(c∗, u)). When Rt ≥0.60 the platform triggers an Echo Meter warning survey (EMA Layer 2); when Rt ≥0.75, Algorithmic Cooling activates and the recommendation switches to maximum diversity, a proposed interpretation of the EST-P2 counterforce, not a veried implementation or measured eect. 4.4 Propaganda Detection and Algorithmic Moderation Every content item is scored on seven features: citation velocity, quality-weighted entropy, semantic fear bias, propagation acceleration, institutional concentration (HHI), predatory-source ratio, and correction velocity. The specication uses a logistic score, ˆp(c) = σ(θ⊤f(c)), and combines it with a temporal anomaly score. A logistic transformation alone does not establish probability calibration; a separate calibration dataset and assessment would be needed before describing the output as calibrated. The proposed combined index is Pprop(c) = 0.7 ˆp(c) + 0.3 ϕTIS(c). (4.7) If Pprop > 0.70 the item receives a visibility penalty, an applied Moderation Cost Ea,mod = λ1(Pprop −0.70) embedded in the feed rank. This is a proposed ranking penalty, not an established economic welfare correction or a calibrated probability of intent. The anomaly score must also be bounded on [0, 1] for the combined index to remain in that range. These author-dened thresholds require evaluation. If the score exceeds 0.85 the item is escalated to ERIC for human review and the broadcast

CHAPTER 4. THE LOKLOK PLATFORM: ARCHITECTURE AND IMPLEMENTATION 69 logs a BRS information-quality penalty. 4.5 The ERIC Governance Loop ERIC is the platform's integrity controller. It monitors ve health indicators (lterbubble score, information diversity, inequality of reputation, detection accuracy, platform sentiment) and selects the minimum-cost intervention, a diversity injection, a friction pause, or a human review, whenever a threshold is crossed. The intended decision rule is to compare changes in a specied governance objective, with its components, scales, and costs recorded. A decrease in the candidate Hamiltonian is not by itself evidence of improved credibility or factual accuracy. Any use of the entropy-regularised objective must separately dene the loss and source distribution, as in Appendix E. An anti-bot module assigns cryptographic identities, monitors behavioural ngerprints, and ags coordination patterns (Luceri et al., 2023); its output feeds the reputation and moderation subsystems rather than making autonomous removal decisions. 4.6 Measurement Surface The platform specication includes the following measurement services. They describe the wider design, not a claim that every service was used in the present cross-sectional survey. In particular, the eld sample is not a session-randomised trial, and no weekly or pre-broadcast panel results are added by describing these capabilities:  Layer 1 Post-broadcast micro-survey (PB1PB5): red within sec-

They are relevant here only as candidate features or controls in the prospective extension. 4.8 Domain Model and Data Flow The following entities describe a proposed shared schema for the platform and model. They do not establish that the historical engine and actual backend use identical data transformations. The core entities are: User (identity, career phase, institution); Broadcaster (a user with a BRS trajectory); Broadcast (session, schedule slot, transcript embedding, source list); Rating (the post-broadcast micro-survey and star record); EchoSample (the Echo Meter rolling values and EMA trigger history); and GovernanceEvent (moderation, anti-bot, and ERIC ledger records). The intended experimental event ow connects assignment, content exposure, rating, feedback, and logged outcomes. In the supplied source these are separate routes and services, not a demonstrated end-to-end G0/G1 experiment. Per-user A/B assignment and the radio service's shared current arm are separate states. The feed ranking path does not read the stored assignment. Consequently, assignment alone does not establish that a user received the intended intervention. The proposed study identies treatment by both the assigned conguration and recorded exposures, with

This mapping is not evidence that each feature was independently experienced or evaluated by all 52 respondents. The eld questionnaire concerns audience evaluations, whereas feature exposure, implementation delity, and event-level behavior require their own records. The calibrated model in Chapter 5 represents selected mechanisms on a simulated substrate, not an additional eld sample. Software implementation, measurement validity, and benecial audience effects are separate accomplishments. A working classier needs labelled evaluation data and calibration checks before its output can be interpreted as a probability of misinformation. A reputation formula needs range, monotonicity, sensitivity, and fairness checks before consequential deployment. For example, placing community validation in a denominator does not by itself guarantee that greater validation increases a score. Human review and documented appeal routes remain necessary design safeguards. These requirements do not change the historical model outputs reported in Chapter 6. 4.11 Correction, Provenance, and Governance Feedback Figure 4.4 applies the event notation of Section 3.3 to correction. A ag is not a nding of falsehood, and a published correction is not evidence of acceptance. Ecker et al. (2022) motivate separating correction exposure from belief revision; the diagram is this thesis's design mapping, not their eect estimate. The proposed system should log review reasons, evidence, decisions, revised versions, and notication routes. Reputation changes must distinguish an original

Accountable moderation also includes an appeal process. A classier score or majority vote is not itself veried factual accuracy. Slower resharing can reect friction rather than better judgment. A shared station and an individual feed dene different exposure units: a station change aects co-listeners, whereas a feed change may be account-specic. The experiment must record both network membership and delivered exposure rather than infer treatment from an assignment label alone. No eld and synthetic records are pooled. 4.13.1 Assignment and Treatment Delivery The restored implementation must map G0 and G1 to explicit features, isolate condition state, and log the content and feedback actually delivered. Historical A/B software labels are not assumed to match the simulation's G0/G1 labels. An adapter must validate allowed actions against the real backend contract; this thesis does not invent executable routes. Each paired run starts from matched recorded state and a frozen roster. The inference unit is an independently reset network pair, not an individual action. 4.13.2 Measurement Identity The administered PB questionnaire, platform EMA windows, scalar feedback, component BRS, and prospective NMLS assessment need separate schema identiers. Original answers must be retained before normalization or aggregation. A 15 star

CHAPTER 4. THE LOKLOK PLATFORM: ARCHITECTURE AND IMPLEMENTATION 80 rating cannot be passed unchanged to a feedback function expecting values in [0, 1]. The transformation must be declared, tested, and logged. No transformation alone establishes measurement validity. 4.13.3 Readiness Criteria Before a live run, verify authentication, condition isolation, action logging, versioned content, independent assessment keys, prohibited-information access, retry limits, and failure handling. A successful test establishes only the behavior it observes. Model identity, prompts, source access, resource budgets, and actual served versions remain part of the execution record. No provider API call or platform run has been performed for this document revision. Chapter summary. The platform chapter species the architecture and the eld interface. BRS, MORE, ERIC, moderation, and the measurement surface are dened, and the interface screens show how they were presented. The chapter is explicit that the interface is a protocol instrument, not proof that every service was used in the eld wave; implementation evidence has limits.
